key_insight: A transformer-based model can infer binary hand-object contact from RGB-D vision plus proprioception, providing a pseudo-tactile signal without dedicated tactile sensors.
engineering_relevance: This offers a lower-cost, more scalable sensing alternative for dexterous manipulation systems, especially where tactile hardware is fragile, expensive, or difficult to integrate.
method: Fuse RGB-D observations with robot proprioception in a multimodal transformer.
Predict binary contact states for hand-object interactions as a learned pseudo-tactile signal.
Use the contact predictions to support reinforcement learning for in-hand object reorientation, including generalization to novel objects.
evidence_signal: The paper reports training a single contact prediction model across multiple objects and validating it in both simulation and on a real robot, with downstream RL performance on in-hand reorientation.
watch_item: Contact is estimated as a binary signal from perception rather than measured directly, so robustness may depend on sensing quality, object appearance, and the limits of generalization to unseen setups.
paper_title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
